subject: surgery
title: Venous Ulcer, Compression and Deep Vein Thrombosis

steps.tx: A chronic skin break above the ankle from venous hypertension is a **venous ulcer**. It sits in the gaiter area, has sloping edges and a granulating base. Surrounding skin shows pigmentation and eczema from years of high venous pressure. A punched out, painful ulcer over a toe or the heel should not be compressed until arterial supply is proven adequate.
steps.say: A venous ulcer breaks skin in the gaiter area from years of high venous pressure.

steps.tx: Brown pigmentation with hard woody skin around the ankle is **lipodermatosclerosis**. Chronic inflammation scars fat and skin into an inverted champagne bottle shape. It often precedes ulceration and signals severe venous disease. The champagne bottle leg narrows at the ankle from scarring while the calf stays full, a shape patients often describe themselves.
steps.say: Lipodermatosclerosis hardens ankle skin into a champagne bottle shape before ulceration.

steps.tx: Graduated external pressure forming the mainstay of ulcer healing is **compression therapy**. Bandages or stockings squeeze hardest at the ankle, pushing blood upward. Arterial supply must be checked first, because compression harms ischaemic legs. An ankle brachial index between 0.8 and 1.3 is the usual safety window for full compression.
steps.say: Compression therapy squeezes hardest at the ankle to heal ulcers, after checking arterial supply first.

steps.tx: The international staging system for venous disease is the **CEAP classification**. It records clinical signs, cause, anatomy and pathophysiology. Higher clinical classes progress from thread veins to active ulceration. Clinical classes run C0 to C6, with C5 a healed ulcer and C6 an active ulcer, a coding examiners expect precisely.
steps.say: The CEAP classification stages venous disease from thread veins to active ulceration.

vis.alt: CEAP classification of venous disease progression.
vis.caption: CEAP classification stages. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Clot formation in the deep veins of the leg is **deep vein thrombosis**. Calf pain and swelling follow, and fragments can travel to the lungs as embolism. Anticoagulation prevents extension while the body dissolves clot. Wells scoring plus D dimer testing decides who needs a scan, and a negative D dimer in a low probability patient avoids imaging.
steps.say: Deep vein thrombosis clots leg veins and can embolise to the lungs without anticoagulation.

steps.tx: Massive iliofemoral thrombosis making the leg swollen, pale and painful is **phlegmasia alba dolens**. Its blue congested progression, phlegmasia cerulea dolens, threatens the limb itself. Both need urgent anticoagulation and specialist review. Cerulea dolens can progress to venous gangrene, and thrombolysis or surgical clot removal enters discussion for the threatened leg.
steps.say: Massive deep thrombosis turns the leg pale then blue and threatened, needing urgent specialist care.

steps.tx: Compression of the left iliac vein by the right iliac artery is **May-Thurner syndrome**. It causes left sided deep vein thrombosis in younger patients. Stenting the compressed vein may follow clot treatment. It explains recurrent left leg clots in young women, sometimes first declared during pregnancy or on the contraceptive pill.
steps.say: May-Thurner syndrome compresses the left iliac vein and causes left sided thrombosis in younger patients.

steps.tx: Healing a venous ulcer also requires treating reflux, a combined approach of **compression plus ablation**. Closing faulty surface veins after healing reduces recurrence greatly. Ulcers that fail to shrink need biopsy to exclude cancer. Ulcers present over twelve weeks, or shrinking less than half by four weeks of good compression, need biopsy.
steps.say: Compression plus ablation after healing cuts ulcer recurrence, and non healing ulcers need biopsy.

vis.alt: Endovenous ablation to prevent ulcer recurrence.
vis.caption: Ablation preventing ulcer recurrence. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Long term stocking use after healing prevents return, termed **recurrence prevention**. Leg elevation, walking and skin care support the stockings. Annual review catches early skin change before breakdown. About a quarter recur within a year without stockings, and closing reflux roughly halves that figure.
steps.say: Recurrence prevention uses stockings, elevation, walking and skin care after ulcer healing.
